words.definition: worthy of praise; deserving approval
words.example: Helping a new student feel welcome is a commendable act.
examples: The team made a commendable effort even though they lost.
Returning the lost wallet was a commendable thing to do.

words.definition: great damage or destruction
words.example: The storm left devastation across the small town.
examples: The flood caused terrible devastation to the farms.
Firefighters surveyed the devastation after the wildfire.

words.definition: not complete; only part of something
words.example: The teacher gave us a partial list of the questions.
examples: We could see only a partial view of the stage.
The puzzle was still partial because three pieces were missing.

words.definition: to remember something
words.example: I can recall the story we read last week.
examples: She could recall every detail of her favorite trip.
Try to recall where you last saw your keys.

words.definition: good at finding clever ways to solve problems
words.example: The resourceful hikers made a shelter from branches.
examples: A resourceful cook can make a meal from almost anything.
Being resourceful, she fixed the kite with tape and string.

words.definition: in a clear, bright, or detailed way
words.example: She vividly described the fireworks in the night sky.
examples: He vividly remembered the smell of the bakery.
The author vividly painted the scene with her words.

words.definition: to make something stand out or seem stronger
words.example: The dark frame accentuates the bright painting.
examples: Bright lights accentuate the colors of the stage.
A good title can accentuate the main idea of a story.

words.definition: a person's usual mood, attitude, or nature
words.example: His cheerful disposition made everyone smile.
examples: The puppy had a gentle, friendly disposition.
Her calm disposition helped the team stay relaxed.

words.definition: great beauty or magnificence
words.example: The splendor of the palace amazed the visitors.
examples: We stared at the splendor of the golden sunset.
The splendor of the mountains left the travelers speechless.

words.definition: a person or animal in a story, play, or movie
words.example: The main character learns an important lesson.
examples: My favorite character in the book is the clever fox.
Each character in the tale has a different problem to solve.

words.definition: to hold something tightly in place
words.example: Dad clamped the wood to the table before cutting it.
examples: She clamped the papers together so they would not blow away.
The crab can clamp its claw shut very tightly.

words.definition: to interest someone very much
words.example: The old legend fascinated the whole class.
examples: Glowing deep-sea fish fascinate many scientists.
Magic tricks fascinate children and adults alike.

words.definition: willing to give or share more than expected
words.example: Her generous friend shared his snack with everyone.
examples: The generous neighbor donated boxes of food to the shelter.
A generous tip made the waiter smile.

words.definition: juicy and tender; full of moisture
words.example: The succulent peach was sweet and fresh.
examples: We bit into the succulent slices of watermelon.
The succulent fruit dripped juice down his chin.

words.definition: careful about spending money or using resources
words.example: A thrifty shopper compares prices before buying.
examples: Being thrifty, the family reused jars instead of buying new ones.
A thrifty traveler packs snacks to avoid buying costly food.

words.definition: to think something is true without being sure
words.example: Do not assume the answer before you read the question.
examples: Do not assume the path is safe just because it looks easy.
I assume you finished your homework, but please check.

words.definition: a feeling of thankfulness
words.example: She showed gratitude by writing a thank-you note.
examples: He felt deep gratitude toward the stranger who helped him.
The villagers expressed their gratitude with a feast.

words.definition: to succeed, grow, or do well
words.example: The small garden prospered in the warm sunshine.
examples: The town began to prosper after the new road was built.
Honest, hard-working people prosper in the old tale.

words.definition: careless about danger or consequences
words.example: Riding a bike without looking is reckless.
examples: The reckless driver sped through the busy street.
It was reckless to swim out so far during the storm.

words.definition: very hot
words.example: We stayed inside during the scorching afternoon.
examples: The scorching sand burned our bare feet.
Travelers crossed the scorching desert before dawn to stay cool.

words.definition: to dry up, shrink, or lose freshness
words.example: The flowers began to wither without water.
examples: The leaves withered in the long, dry summer.
Without care, even the strongest plant will wither.
